title: Trump Says He Would Certainly Consider Military Force Against Cuba
summary: President Donald Trump tells a Salem News Channel interview that he would certainly consider military force against Cuba before leaving office. Several outlets quote the November 12, 2026 remarks, and the Clash Report carries the earliest timestamp found.
contents:
## Event

President Donald Trump says he wants to 'get Cuba done' before he leaves office and that he would 'certainly consider' using military force against the island. Hugh Hewitt put the question during a Salem News Channel interview, and several outlets quote the answer from Trump directly. Trump describes Cuba as a 'failed' nation and names Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a 'very good, talented guy for Cuba' who 'would love to do that.'

## Location and Time

The reported statement concerns Cuba as a whole, so the map point uses the Cuba country centroid rather than a city. The interview took place on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The earliest outlet timestamp located, from the Clash Report, reads 20:48 GMT, which this record stores as 2026-11-12T20:48:00Z. The point marks the subject nation only; it does not mark any planned operational location.

## Evidence

The primary evidence comes from the recorded telephone interview with Trump on Salem News Channel, which the Clash Report quotes as saying he would 'certainly consider that, yes.' Breaking the News, G1, Infobae, and The New Republic also quote the same interview. Because these outlets repeat one original remark, this record does not count them as independent corroboration. The Intel Slava Z (@intelslava) Telegram post relays the remark at 21:01:56 UTC, after the earliest outlet timestamp. No official White House transcript appeared in the sources checked during qualification.

## Allied Relevance

The stated willingness of Trump to use force against Cuba bears directly on United States and allied planning for Caribbean security, migration flows, and sanctions enforcement. Partner governments track this rhetoric because existing US fuel restrictions on the island, together with the recent US capture of Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela, form the context for the threat. The statement offers situational awareness of the publicly stated intent of an official. It describes no order, deployment, or strike.

## Confidence and Gaps

Confidence rests on direct quotations from a recorded interview that several outlets reproduce. The timestamp gives minutes only, and the broadcast itself carries no published time, so an earlier original report remains possible. The remarks express conditional intent rather than a decision or an order. Cuban officials had issued no immediate public response when the Clash Report published its account, and no later Cuban reaction appeared in the sources checked.
allied_relevance: A stated US presidential willingness to use force against Cuba informs United States and allied threat, migration, and sanctions planning.
